name: Vail
overview: The vail in Scripture is described as a finely crafted hanging made of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen with cherubim, skillfully made by Bezaleel and Aholiab to separate the Holy of Holies from the Holy Place in the tabernacle (Exodus 26:31; 36:35). It also served as a covering for the ark of the covenant, symbolizing the sacred separation between God's presence and the people (Exodus 35:12; 40:21). Notably, the temple vail was torn from top to bottom at the crucifixion of Jesus, a profound event that carries deep figurative significance, marking the removal of the barrier between God and humanity.
